channel.title: AffineDrift
channel.description: Affine control theory for golf swing dynamics - Research articles, models, and resources

item.title: Theory Part 1 — State definition and affine derivation
item.description: Establishes the multibody coordinates, derives the control-affine structure, and sets the notation used in every subsequent article.

item.title: Theory Part 2 — Drift/input decomposition, ZTCF, ZVCF
item.description: Formalizes how to separate passive dynamics from deliberate torque using zero torque and zero velocity counterfactuals.

item.title: Theory Part 3 — Drift invariance and taxonomy
item.description: Explores invariants, introduces a force taxonomy, and discusses limitations of the affine assumption.

item.title: Theory Part 4 — Modal Approximation, Wrenches, and Pendulum Dynamics
item.description: Collects derivations, modal approximations, and pendulum examples that support the main theory.

item.title: Theory Part 5 — Simulink Model Documentation
item.description: Documents the Simulink implementation, numerical routines, and supporting technical notes.

item.title: Interpretation of Inverse Dynamics
item.description: Shows why inverse dynamics results require careful interpretation and how counterfactuals resolve the force-couple ambiguity.

item.title: Wrists behave as universal joints
item.description: Analysis of wrist biomechanics showing how wrists function as universal joints in golf swing dynamics.

item.title: Nonlinear Control Insights
item.description: Insights into nonlinear control theory and its applications to biomechanical systems.
